key_insight: The paper shows that LLM-agent safety for mission-critical workflows needs joint spatial, temporal, and semantic runtime checks, because single-aspect or pairwise guards can miss multi-step violation chains.
engineering_relevance: A policy can be enforced at the agent–system interface without retraining the model, making this approach practical for procured LLM components in safety- and defense-oriented settings.
method: Decompose each natural-language rule into a typed spatial/temporal/semantic triple over one canonical event stream.
Monitor the temporal aspect with MonPoly and interpret spatial obligations on a weighted two-sorted location graph.
Fuse aspect verdicts with a four-valued provenance-carrying algebra to decide blocking/allowing actions.
evidence_signal: Across casualty evacuation, contested sustainment, and one civil domain, the full composed monitor drove attack success to zero with no observed false positives and microsecond-scale per-event overhead.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees depend on accurate policy decomposition and a well-specified canonical event stream, so deployment complexity and spec-mapping errors are key risks.
paper_title: Multi-Aspect Runtime Verification for Simulation-Based V&V of LLM-Enabled Autonomous Agents
